Subject: Severe latency & 500 spikes in AZ4 - need immediate routing help

Karthik / Redwood team,

We started seeing a sharp increase in end-to-end latency from our Summit Health 3P traffic routed to AZ4 around 08:45 PDT this morning. Error rates jumped to ~9% (mostly 500/502) and P95 latencies spiked to ~3.2s from our baseline of ~350ms. Our health checks are starting to mark backends unhealthy and customers are reporting slow triage flows.

I attached a short capture and a screenshot of our monitoring (error_snapshot.png). Can you confirm whether this is a regional routing issue or something on the model/infra side? We need a timeline for mitigation and whether you can divert traffic to another region while you investigate.

We are escalating to our ops and procurement — copying James and TechOps. Please advise next steps immediately; this is impacting patient intake.

Thanks,
Sarah Ortega
Director, Technical Integrations
Summit Health

Thanks for flagging, Sarah — sorry you’re seeing this. I’m escalating internally and we’ll execute an immediate routing diversion to reduce customer impact while we investigate root cause. High level plan now: 

- Immediate (T+10m): Start staged cross-region diversion from AZ4 -> US-WEST-2 with traffic shaping at 20% increments to avoid cold KV cache pressure.
- T+30m: Hold and monitor error and latency delta; if P95 improves and 500s drop, continue to 100%.
- T+60-120m: If stable, leave diversion active and continue deep triage of AZ4 nodes (kernel/PCIe errors, NVLINK logs, autoscaler behavior).

Hannah, can you own the diversion play and post a short checklist in the runbook link? Marissa — I’ll need executive authorization for cross-region failover and approval to offer a one-time service credit (since SLOs breached) if Summit wants it. Vanessa, please coordinate communications with the customer and copy legal if they request contract language.

Sarah, I’ve put this as P0 and I’ll be your exec liaison. I’ll update every 30 minutes and we’ll schedule a postmortem after stabilization.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Cell: +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:41:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Severe latency & 500 spikes in AZ4 - need immediate routing help

Karthik — taking point on the diversion. Quick technical summary from initial triage: 

- Observable: 08:42 PDT spike in 500/502 across frontends that terminate on AZ4 pool group AH-az4-prod. Kernel logs show repeated NVME I/O timeouts on three nodes and a spike in KV cache eviction.
- Hypothesis: A partial rack-level storage performance degradation causing request timeouts and amplification of tail latency under continuous batching.

Immediate actions I’m executing now:
1) Kickstage diversion to US-WEST-2 (start 20% at 09:45 PDT).
2) Isolate affected AZ4 instances from the public routing table (drain) and trigger live diagnostics (pci-stress, iostat collection).
3) Disable aggressive continuous-batching for Summit routes to avoid large KV cache pressure until cache warms in target region.

Metrics to watch: 500-rate, P95, KV-cache-miss-rate, and process restarts. I’ll paste a small excerpt from the routing logs below (truncated):

--- routing log (az4) ---
[09:42:11] front-az4-12 -> backend-az4-07 502 latency=3121ms status=502
[09:42:12] front-az4-03 -> backend-az4-14 500 latency=2988ms status=500
[09:42:13] front-az4-09 -> backend-az4-07 200 latency=345ms status=200
--- end ---

I’ll confirm when 20% divert is live and push a monitoring dashboard link. If P95 remains >1s after 2 increments, we should consider a faster cutover.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
